title: What if all three corners of a triangle lie on one line?
description: A wooden roof frame is shown, and its three beams are drawn as the three sides of a triangle. The three corners then slide towards one straight line, and the video stops on the question of what happens to the frame.
teaching_notes: One idea: three straight pieces joined at their ends make a triangle only when the three corners do not lie on one line. Ask each child to say what they expect and why, and do not confirm or reject any answer, because the next topics settle it. Watch for children who say the frame always keeps three corners.

video_script.why: Before any rule on triangles, the child sees the three corners and three sides of a triangle and wonders what happens when the corners lie on one line.
video_script.substitution: The three beams of a roof frame stand for the three sides, and their joints stand for the three corners.
video_script.anchor: A wooden roof frame whose three beams are the three sides of a triangle, with the three corners free to slide onto one line
maths_rules: A triangle has three corners and three straight sides that join the corners in pairs.
The open question: what happens when the three corners lie on one straight line. No answer is shown or hinted.
video_script.design: One idea: a triangle has three corners and three sides, and the corners could be made to lie on one line. The photo opens the video and fades; the drawn frame carries the question; the answer is never shown.
